articles.description: Data centres are the lifeblood of our digital world, but there are growing concerns about their environmental impact. The BBC explores their rise in charts.
articles.summary: Until a few years ago many of us may have been blissfully unaware of what a data centre was.
key_points: These giant, warehouse-like buildings power virtually all our internet activity, from our web searches and emails to movie downloads and online banking.
They are at the heart of the AI boom, housing the advanced computer chips and servers needed to run services like ChatGPT and Claude.
But the speed at which they're growing, the enormous amount of electricity they consume and concerns about their environmental impact are fuelling a public backlash around the world.

articles.title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm
articles.description: Scotland editor James Cook finds out what life is like on board a ship in an untapped oil field awaiting its fate.
articles.summary: When we landed by helicopter at Rosebank, this oil field was at the centre of a political storm - and set to be in the path of a real one.
key_points: We arrived on Wednesday morning, just a few hours after the UK government had granted consent for the production of gas from the Jackdaw field in the North Sea.
But already attention was shifting to this wild and windy patch of the North Atlantic – the next big decision for Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh.
Rosebank is bigger than Jackdaw, it would generate higher greenhouse gas emissions, and it could be far more lucrative for its owners, Adura and Ithaca.

articles.title: Will a new code end 'rip-off parking charges'?

articles.summary: Rosey Greenwood was asked to pay £1,906 because she took more than five minutes to pay for parking "I was completely on edge, every single day," said Rosey Greenwood.
key_points: "I had letters coming through - I had debt collectors after me." Two years ago, Rosey was being told to pay £1,906 because she had taken too long to pay for parking.
Rosey had paid every single time she parked at the Copeland Street car park in Derby, and had bank records to prove it.
But Rosey had unknowingly broken the car park's terms and conditions, which stipulated that drivers must pay within five minutes of entering.
